$comment: Bounds here mirror runtime/mvp_runtime/crypto/guards.py — the module that owns the numbers. Both must agree; the builder checks the code bounds first so a refusal names the offending limit instead of emitting a raw schema error.
title: Crypto Risk Limits v0.1
description: An operator-registered, self-hashed override of the C4 risk-breaker limits (daily/weekly R loss, consecutive losses, drawdown, risk-per-trade). Without one, the runtime judges on the guards.py defaults. Registering one grants nothing and enables no trading: it can only move a breaker inside the code-enforced relaxation bounds, and the live-trading grant, confirmation phrase, canary evidence and registered budget all still stand between here and a live order. The record carries a validity window on purpose — a relaxation expires and reverts to a REFUSAL, never silently back to the defaults.

limits.description: All five breakers, every one required. A partial override would leave the unnamed limits implicit, so the record states the whole set — what judged a cycle is then readable from the record alone.

risk_per_trade.description: Equity fraction risked per trade, used to map the drawdown percent into R. Ceiling 0.02 (2x the 0.01 default).

daily_max_loss_r.description: Daily realized-loss breaker in R. Negative; floor -6.0 (3x the -2.0 default). Must not be looser than weekly_max_loss_r (cross-field, enforced by the builder).

weekly_max_loss_r.description: Weekly realized-loss breaker in R. Negative; floor -15.0 (3x the -5.0 default).

max_consecutive_losses.description: Consecutive-loss breaker. At least 1 (0 would read as unconfigured = always breached); ceiling 10.

max_drawdown_pct.description: Current-drawdown-from-peak breaker, in equity percent. Negative; floor -25.0 (2.5x the -10.0 default).

drawdown_baseline_rebase.description: OPTIONAL. Narrows the population the DRAWDOWN breaker measures, and nothing else — daily, weekly and consecutive-loss still judge every closed outcome. Absent means today's behaviour exactly: the drawdown is measured over the whole own-paper record. The rule it encodes is closed in both directions and the guard, not this record, applies it: an outcome leaves the baseline only if it NAMES a lineage, that lineage is listed here, AND that lineage is not currently routable in the active pool. A row that cannot name its lineage never leaves; a lineage that is re-promoted silently invalidates its own exclusion and its outcomes return to the drawdown. This record supplies data; the predicate is re-evaluated every cycle against the live pool, so the failure direction is toward putting losses back.

excluded_strategy_ids.description: Strategy ids whose closed outcomes may leave the drawdown baseline, subject to the guard's own re-check that none of them is currently routable. The pool's own key, so 'is this lineage still being routed' is a lookup rather than an inference.

reason.description: Why this set was retired, in the operator's own words. A rebase is a mechanism for forgetting losses; the record has to say whose, and why, or the ledger cannot be re-read later.
